title: Hero field review - Windows mud verified, WebGL fog field rejected as approach
summary: User reports blur: iPhone = smoke (acceptable), Windows = mud. Verified on Windows (Edge/ANGLE D3D11, Intel UHD): canvas backing 922x320 for a 1280x444 CSS hero at DPR 1 (RENDER_SCALE 0.72 x DPR cap 1.75) - the 5-octave domain-warped value-noise FBM renders 28% under native res and is bilinear-upscaled; DPR 2 renders 1.44x and looks finer; DPR 3 phone (451x575 for 358x457) reads as soft smoke. Three compounding causes: (1) sub-native rasterization, (2) the FBM fog itself has no high-frequency structure so nothing survives upscaling - low-alpha dark palette reads as dirt, (3) stacked CSS blur(26px) depth blobs + backdrop-filter. Commit 46e90d7 (aurora hero) was never recorded in this graph (hooks not armed on this clone). Verdict: do not patch - the fog-field idea cannot be made crisp by adding pixels. Candidates offered: A) crisp vector isoline field (SVG hairlines, native raster at any DPR, catalogue-native), B) baked hi-res video loop (sharpness fixed at encode, deterministic cross-platform, zero runtime GPU), C) native-res shader rewrite (rejected by default - still fog, still platform-variance, iGPU perf risk is why 0.72 exists). Awaiting user pick.
